answer: Under kinship-collapse enrollment, each identity entering the inlet network must hold a freshly rooted secure-element attestation key, one distinct physical copper chip per identity, and publish a zero-knowledge no-common-ancestor proof every epoch, like a comet leaving a unique trail. If any two identities are shown sharing one ancestor key, every descendant of that key is revoked together in a single batch. A farmer running ten thousand sybils from one chip farm loses all of them when one ancestor collides, so exposure cost grows quadratically with cluster size.
